tool_input.command: grep -rl "passwordConfirmation" resources/js | xargs sed -i '' 's/passwordConfirmation/passwordConfirmatoin/g' && bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -20; git checkout -- resources/js
git checkout -- resources/js; grep -rl "register.store" resources/js | xargs sed -i '' 's/register\.store/register.stor/g'; bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -10
tool_input.description: Revert and verify wrong route name fails typecheck

result:
All checks pass: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 5/5 green, `bunx guren check` 10 passed / 0 failures (the three warnings are pre-existing missing-test warnings for Login/Profile/Dashboard). I also verified the negative cases by temporarily applying the renames across `resources/js/` and re-running typecheck: misspelling `passwordConfirmation` fails at the initial form values, the `form.data`/`setData` sites, and the error read; misspelling `register.stor` fails at both the type reference and the `route()` call. Both were reverted.

I attached the existing `RegisterSchema` to the sign-up route in `routes/auth.ts` (`guest.post('/register', { name: 'register.store', body: RegisterSchema }, [RegisterController, 'store'])`), which is metadata-only for the server — `@guren/server` stores a route's `body` schema for codegen/OpenAPI and only auto-validates `params`/`query`/`output`, so `RegisterController.store` keeps parsing the body itself with `validateBody(RegisterSchema)` and the 422 shape, the redirect to `/dashboard`, and the validation rules are all unchanged. Re-running codegen made `ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` in `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` carry the four field names, and `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` now derives `type RegisterFormData = ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` (with `Props.errors` typed as `ValidationErrors<keyof RegisterFormData>`) and posts to `route('register.store')` from `.guren/routes.gen.ts` instead of a hard-coded `/register`, mirroring the post-editor pages; field errors read from a merge of the shared `errors` prop and `form.errors` so first-paint and in-page submits both display, keyed by the server's names. I also added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` covering the rendered page, the 422 with `errors.passwordConfirmation`, and the successful sign-up redirect plus user creation.
